apps.title: Run a node
apps.body: Pick where to run a node: install an app or the command line node, or open the web node in a browser. Each one joins a pool with a code from Add device.

mobile.title: Mobile app
mobile.body: Turn an Android phone into an always-on node. It keeps serving with the screen off.

desktop.title: Desktop app
desktop.body: Serve from a Linux, macOS (Apple silicon) or Windows computer. It runs in the system tray and updates itself.

cli.title: Command line
cli.body: Run a node on a server or any computer without a screen. Install it with one command, then join with a code from Add device.

web.title: Web node
web.body: No install: open the web node in a browser tab and join with a code. It only serves while the tab stays open.

home.title: Put idle devices to work
home.subtitle: Turn the phones, laptops and Raspberry Pis you already own into inference nodes. Group them into pools and serve models through one OpenAI-compatible API.
trust: Runs on phones, laptops, Pis and browsers

how.title: From idle hardware to an API in three steps
how.subtitle: No servers to rent, no ports to open.

one.title: Enroll your devices
one.body: Create a short code in the app and type it in, or scan its QR with the device. The device connects out to the gateway and is ready.

two.title: Pick a model and a pool
two.body: Add a LiteRT-LM model by link or upload its .litertlm file, then assign it to a pool. Every device in the pool downloads and serves it.

three.title: Call the API
three.body: Create an API key and point any OpenAI client at the gateway. Requests are balanced across your healthy devices.

features.title: A complete serving platform, not just a connection
features.subtitle: The control plane and the gateway run for you. You bring the compute.

pools.title: Pools and models
pools.body: Group devices per organisation. Each pool serves one model, replicated on every device.

enroll.title: Enroll with a short code
enroll.body: Phones, laptops, servers and browser tabs join in seconds, with optional admin approval.

api.title: OpenAI-compatible API
api.body: Change only the base URL and API key. Streaming, images and audio input are supported.

security.title: Secure by design
security.body: Each device has its own key, the gateway is verified independently of TLS, and API keys are stored hashed.

limits.title: Rate limits
limits.body: Cap requests and tokens per key or per organisation, and get a clear 429 when a limit is hit.

insights.title: Usage and benchmarks
insights.body: See tokens per key and pool, and measure latency and tokens per second on your real devices.

code.title: Works with the tools you already use
code.body: Same request format, same streaming. Swap the base URL and you are done.

run.title: Pick where to run a node
run.subtitle: Install an app or the command line node, or open the web node in a browser. Each one joins a pool with a code from Add device.

cta.title: Ready to put your devices to work?
cta.body: Create an organisation, enroll a device and make your first request in minutes.

hero.lead: SplitCortex is a platform that reuses the devices you already own as inference serving nodes. We run the control plane and the gateway; you bring the phones, laptops and Raspberry Pis.

story.title: Billions of capable devices sit idle
story.problem: Phones and small computers now run capable language models, yet most of them spend the day idle in a drawer or on a desk. Renting GPUs in a datacenter is costly, and sending private prompts to someone else's hardware is not always an option.
story.answer: Turn those devices into a pool you control. Each device keeps one outbound, encrypted connection to our gateway, which receives OpenAI-format requests and relays them to a healthy device in your pool. Your hardware, your models, one familiar API.

flow.title: How a request travels
flow.subtitle: Two separate legs, kept apart on purpose: your client talks to the gateway, and your devices talk to the gateway. Nothing ever connects into a device.

client.title: Your application
client.body: Any OpenAI client or plain HTTP call, authenticated with an API key.

gateway.title: Gateway
gateway.body: Handles every request in four steps.
steps: Route to a healthy node in the pool

node.title: Your device
node.body: Runs LiteRT-LM models on the device and streams tokens back over its single connection.

principles.title: Built to be trusted with your prompts
principles.subtitle: Security and privacy are part of the architecture, not a feature list.

byod.title: Your devices, your data
byod.body: Compute comes from hardware you own and enroll, so prompts never run on strangers' devices.

outbound.title: Outbound only
outbound.body: Devices dial out over TLS. There is no port to open and no inbound access to a phone or a laptop.

identity.title: Verified identities
identity.body: Every device generates its own key and proves it on connect. Devices pin the gateway's key and check it independently of the certificate chain.

keys.title: Keys never stored in clear
keys.body: API keys are stored only as hashes and shown once. Device credentials can be revoked one by one.

tenants.title: Tenant isolation
tenants.body: Every query, device stream and registry entry is scoped to an organisation.

privacy.title: No prompt logging
privacy.body: Prompts and completions are never logged. Benchmarks only use prompts we supply.

nodes.title: Runs on what you have
nodes.subtitle: Every node enrolls with the same short code and serves the same way.

mobile.title: Android phone
mobile.body: A background service keeps serving with the screen off, and starts on boot.

desktop.title: Desktop app
desktop.body: Linux, macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows. Lives in the tray and updates itself.

cli.title: Command line
cli.body: A headless node for servers and Raspberry Pis, installed with one command, optionally as a service.

web.title: Web node
web.body: Nothing to install: a browser tab serves with WebGPU for as long as it stays open.

cta.title: See it for yourself
cta.body: Create an organisation and enroll your first device.
